name: nk3
title: Three-equation New Keynesian (NK) model with an inflation-expectations wedge
description: The small workhorse model central banks use to think about inflation and the business cycle. Demand: households spend more when the real interest rate is low (the IS curve). Supply: firms raise prices faster when demand is strong and when they expect high inflation (the Phillips curve). Policy: the central bank raises the interest rate when inflation or output are high (the Taylor rule). Every variable is a deviation from a steady state with inflation on target, so 0 means normal. All values are decimals per period, 0.01 = 1 percentage point.

beta.description: Discount factor: how much firms and households value next period relative to today.

sigma.description: Inverse intertemporal elasticity of substitution; higher means demand reacts less to the interest rate.

kappa.description: Slope of the Phillips curve: how strongly inflation rises when output is above normal.

phi_pi.description: Central bank reaction to inflation, in points of interest rate per point of inflation; must exceed 1 for stability.

phi_x.description: Central bank reaction to the output gap.

r_n.units: decimal per period, 0 in the steady state
r_n.description: Natural rate of interest or demand shifter: summarises confidence, fiscal policy, credit conditions and saving behaviour that move spending independently of the interest rate.

u.units: decimal per period, 0 in the steady state
u.description: Cost-push shock: a supply-side force that raises firms' prices for given demand, such as an energy price spike or supply-chain disruption.

eps_i.units: decimal per period, 0 in the steady state
eps_i.description: Monetary policy shock: a surprise deviation of the policy rate from what the central bank's rule implies.

wedge_pi.units: decimal per period, 0 in the steady state
wedge_pi.description: Inflation-expectations wedge: how much expected inflation exceeds the model-consistent value; 0 means rational expectations.

x.description: Output gap: how far output is above or below its normal level; found by the solver.

pi.units: decimal per period, 0 in the steady state
pi.description: Inflation as a deviation from the central bank's target; found by the solver.

i.units: decimal per period, 0 in the steady state
i.description: Nominal policy interest rate as a deviation from its steady-state level; found by the solver.

rr.units: decimal per period, 0 in the steady state
rr.description: Ex-post real interest rate: the nominal rate minus next period's inflation.
